import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components'

[Auth.js](https://authjs.dev) signs users in through the [OpenID Provider](/build/openid-provider)
with a [custom OIDC provider](https://authjs.dev/guides/configuring-oauth-providers). Discovery
supplies the endpoints. In the tested version, an `oidc` provider sent PKCE with no extra setting.

<Aside type="note" title="What this was tested against">
  `next-auth` 5.0.0-beta.32 (with `@auth/core` 0.41.3), Next.js 16.4.5 and Node 24, against released
  `seamless-auth-api` v0.22.0 and `seamless-auth-oidc-provider` v0.3.0, on 2026-11-04. Version 5 is
  on npm's `beta` tag. The `latest` tag, 4.24.15, and other Auth.js integrations such as
  `@auth/express` were not tested. Nothing here needs API v0.23.0. See
  [What was and was not tested](#what-was-and-was-not-tested): this is a local test, not production
  verification.
</Aside>

---

## 1. Give The App A Real Hostname, Over HTTPS

<Aside type="caution" title="Next.js cannot use 127.0.0.1 with this provider">
  Next.js rewrites `127.0.0.1` to `localhost` in the URL its route handlers see
  ([`next-url.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/server/web/next-url.ts)),
  even with `AUTH_URL` set. The provider refuses `localhost` as a redirect host, so a client registered
  on `http://127.0.0.1` signs in up to the callback and then fails with `invalid_grant`, because the
  redirect URI at the token endpoint no longer matches. See [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).
</Aside>

So even locally, this app needs `https` on a name that is not `localhost`. The test used
`https://app.guides.test:13443`, with Caddy terminating TLS:

```caddyfile
{
	local_certs
	skip_install_trust
	admin off
	auto_https disable_redirects
}

https://app.guides.test:13443 {
	reverse_proxy authjs:13001
}
```

On your own machine that name needs to resolve to `127.0.0.1`, for example through your hosts file.
The test instead gave Chromium `--host-resolver-rules=MAP *.guides.test 127.0.0.1`.

---

## 2. Register The Client

`POST /admin/applications`. Prefer `private_key_jwt`, which Auth.js supports:

```json
{
  "name": "My Next.js app",
  "clientType": "confidential",
  "firstParty": true,
  "tokenEndpointAuthMethod": "private_key_jwt",
  "jwks": { "keys": [{ "kty": "RSA", "n": "...", "e": "AQAB", "kid": "my-app-1", "alg": "RS256", "use": "sig" }] },
  "redirectUris": ["https://app.guides.test:13443/api/auth/callback/seamless"],
  "postLogoutRedirectUris": ["https://app.guides.test:13443/"],
  "grantTypes": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"]
}
```

The redirect path is `/api/auth/callback/<provider id>`. For a shared secret, use
`client_secret_basic` without `jwks`, after
[turning on `allow_client_secrets`](/build/openid-provider-connect-an-app#register-the-client).

---

## 3. Configure Auth.js

`auth.ts`, with `private_key_jwt`:

```ts
import NextAuth from 'next-auth'

const jwk = JSON.parse(process.env.AUTH_SEAMLESS_PRIVATE_JWK ?? '{}')
const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
  'jwk',
  jwk,
  { name: 'RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5', hash: 'SHA-256' },
  false,
  ['sign'],
)

export const { handlers, auth, signIn, signOut } = NextAuth({
  providers: [
    {
      id: 'seamless',
      name: 'Seamless',
      type: 'oidc',
      issuer: process.env.AUTH_SEAMLESS_ISSUER,
      clientId: process.env.AUTH_SEAMLESS_ID,
      client: { token_endpoint_auth_method: 'private_key_jwt' },
      token: { clientPrivateKey: { key, kid: jwk.kid } },
      authorization: { params: { scope: 'openid email' } },
    },
  ],
  callbacks: {
    jwt({ token, account, profile }) {
      if (account && profile) {
        token.sub = profile.sub ?? token.sub
        token.acr = profile.acr
      }
      return token
    },
    session({ session, token }) {
      session.user.id = token.sub!
      return session
    },
  },
})
```

`token.clientPrivateKey` comes from the
[`@auth/core` source](https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/blob/main/packages/core/src/lib/actions/callback/oauth/callback.ts),
not from the Auth.js guides, so check it again when you upgrade.

With a shared secret, drop the key import, `client` and `token`, and add
`clientSecret: process.env.AUTH_SEAMLESS_SECRET`.

`app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts`:

```ts
import { handlers } from '@/auth'
export const { GET, POST } = handlers
```

Read the session and sign in from a server component:

```tsx
import { auth, signIn, signOut } from '@/auth'

export default async function Page() {
  const session = await auth()
  if (!session?.user) {
    return (
      <form action={async () => { 'use server'; await signIn('seamless') }}>
        <button type="submit">Sign in with Seamless</button>
      </form>
    )
  }
  return <p>Signed in as {session.user.email}</p>
}
```

The provider issues no `name` or `picture` claim, so `session.user.name` and `image` stay empty.

---

## 4. Run It

| Variable                    | Value                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AUTH_URL`                  | `https://app.guides.test:13443`, the app's public origin                    |
| `AUTH_SECRET`               | A random secret for Auth.js's own cookies                                   |
| `AUTH_SEAMLESS_ISSUER`      | The issuer, for example `https://auth.guides.localhost:19443`               |
| `AUTH_SEAMLESS_ID`          | `application.id`                                                            |
| `AUTH_SEAMLESS_PRIVATE_JWK` | The private JWK as JSON, including its `kid`. Or `AUTH_SEAMLESS_SECRET`.    |
| `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`       | Private CA only: the path to the CA file                                    |

See [Auth.js environment variables](https://authjs.dev/getting-started/deployment#environment-variables)
and [`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`](https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#node_extra_ca_certsfile). The test ran
`next build` and `next start -H 0.0.0.0 -p 13001` in a `node:24-alpine` container on the recipe's
compose network.

---

## 5. Check It

1. Open the app and choose **Sign in with Seamless**.
2. Sign in on the hosted page. A first-party client shows no consent page.
3. The app shows `Signed in as <email>`. In the test, `session.user.id` held the `sub`, and `acr` was
   empty after the first email-code sign-up and `phrh` after a passkey sign-in on the virtual
   authenticator.

---

## Sign-Out

`signOut()` ends only the Auth.js session. In the test, the next **Sign in with Seamless** went straight
back to the app without showing the hosted page, because the user's Seamless session was still live.
If your app needs to end that session, send the browser to the provider's
[sign-out endpoint](/build/openid-provider#sign-out) as well. That part was not run with Auth.js. It
was run in the [generic guide](/build/openid-provider-connect-an-app#sign-out).

---

## Troubleshooting

Each of these was hit while testing. Auth.js's detail is in the server log, under `[auth][cause]` and
`[auth][details]`.

| What you see                                                                         | Log line                                                                     | Cause and fix                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Server error`, at `http://localhost:<port>/api/auth/error?error=Configuration`, after the hosted page | `CallbackRouteError` with `"error": "invalid_grant"`, `"grant request is invalid"` | The app runs on `http://127.0.0.1`. See [step 1](#1-give-the-app-a-real-hostname-over-https). `/api/auth/providers` shows the callback URL it uses. |
| Registering returns `localhost is not a redirect host`, for `app.guides.localhost`   | None, it is the registration response                                        | `*.localhost` is refused even over `https`. Use another name, such as one under `.test`.                                                              |
| `Server error`, `error=Configuration`, on choosing sign-in                           | `[auth][error] TypeError: fetch failed`                                      | The app does not trust the issuer's CA. Set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.                                                                                    |
| An error page on `/authorize`, `missing required parameter 'client_id'`              | None                                                                         | `AUTH_SEAMLESS_ID` is empty.                                                                                                                          |

Registration and shared-secret errors are in the
[generic guide](/build/openid-provider-connect-an-app#troubleshooting).

---

## What Was And Was Not Tested

**Tested.** The configuration above, built and started in production mode, once with `private_key_jwt`
and once with `client_secret_basic`, with Playwright's Chromium and a virtual WebAuthn authenticator: a
new user registering and a passkey sign-in from a clean browser, ending on a page showing the user. The
stack was the local recipe from
[seamless-auth-oidc-provider#60](https://github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-oidc-provider/pull/60)
(not merged at the time of writing), adjusted as described in the
[generic guide](/build/openid-provider-connect-an-app#what-was-and-was-not-tested).

**Not tested.** A browser that trusts the CA normally, a real authenticator, a publicly trusted
certificate, a production deployment, `next dev`, refresh tokens or access token rotation in Auth.js,
database sessions, Auth.js middleware, `next-auth` 4, or other Auth.js integrations.
